name: Per-surface usability source audit with adversarial finding verification
description: Audit every UI surface at the SOURCE level for broken or unusable controls, and let no finding enter the fix queue until an adversarial verifier has confirmed it against the source. Two mechanisms carry it. First, the surface inventory comes from the ROUTER, not from clicking, because a conditionally-rendered surface is unreachable by interaction and would otherwise be silently omitted. Second, a SECOND fan-out verifies each finding individually and records the DROPS - in one executed run a large fraction of raw findings did not survive verification, so an unverified queue would have been mostly noise. A surface that cannot be analysed statically is listed UNAUDITED, never clean.

source_root.description: Repository root of the app's UI source. Opened read-only.

router_manifest.description: The route table or equivalent source of truth for what surfaces EXIST. Clicking cannot enumerate conditional surfaces.

verification_standard.description: How strong a finding's proof must be before it may enter the queue.

max_surface_concurrency.description: One agent per surface is expensive; this is the ceiling that keeps a 300-surface app from freezing the box.

surface-enumerator.description: Derives the surface inventory from the router source, not from interaction.

surface-auditor.description: Audits one surface's controls at source level for broken or unusable affordances.

finding-verifier.description: Adversarially re-derives each finding from source. A finding it cannot confirm is DROPPED and the drop is recorded.

ranker.description: Ranks surviving findings into a fix queue by severity times surface reach.

routes.reason: the verifier must fail differently from the auditor that raised the finding

stages.title: S0 - enumerate surfaces from the ROUTER, not from clicking

work_unit.title: Derive the complete surface inventory from the router source of truth
work_unit.question_or_target: Enumerate every surface the router can reach, INCLUDING conditionally-rendered ones that no click sequence can reach, and record for each whether static analysis is possible.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: reading a router to find conditional surfaces requires understanding the guard conditions

work_unit.evidence_requirement: each surface with its router entry file:line, its render guard if any, and an analysable/unanalysable flag with the reason
tests_required: a conditionally-rendered surface unreachable by clicking still appears in the inventory
a surface behind a feature flag is enumerated with its guard recorded, not omitted
both-states control: removing a route from the manifest removes exactly one surface from the inventory
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the finding-verifier, which will reject findings on surfaces the inventory never declared
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:UX-7901 emitted only when every router entry maps to an inventory row carrying an analysable flag; otherwise FAILED:UX-7901 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot to a second enumeration route (a build manifest) rather than re-parsing the same router
work_unit.mechanism: router-derived enumeration that reaches conditionally-rendered surfaces

stages.title: Clicking is not an enumeration - the inventory must come from the router
S1 - one agent per surface, auditing controls at source level

work_unit.title: Audit one surface for broken, dead or unusable controls at source level
work_unit.question_or_target: For one surface, find every control whose handler is missing, unreachable, permanently disabled, or unlabelled, and cite file:line for each - and if the surface cannot be analysed statically, emit UNAUDITED with the reason.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: recognising that a handler is unreachable requires following the control flow, which is judgement

work_unit.evidence_requirement: every finding cites file:line and the defect class; a finding without an anchor is not submittable
tests_required: a control with no handler is found and anchored to file:line
a surface that cannot be statically analysed emits UNAUDITED with a reason, NOT an empty clean result
both-states control: a surface with a known-good control set yields zero findings, so the auditor is not fabricating defects
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:UX-7902 emitted only when the surface has a finding list (possibly empty) or an explicit UNAUDITED reason; otherwise FAILED:UX-7902 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then quarantine the surface as UNAUDITED rather than reporting it clean
work_unit.mechanism: per-surface source-level control audit with UNAUDITED rather than clean-by-default

stages.title: An unanalysable surface is UNAUDITED, never clean
S2 - adversarially verify EACH finding; a drop is recorded, not hidden

body.title: Re-derive one finding from source, independently

work_unit.title: Independently confirm or refute one finding from the cited source
work_unit.question_or_target: Open the cited file:line and decide, without reading the auditor's reasoning, whether the defect is real - and when it is not, record a DROP with the reason so the queue's shrinkage is visible.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: a same-vendor verifier shares the auditor's blind spots; the drop authority must fail differently

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the re-derivation from the cited anchor, and for a refutation the specific reason the defect is not real
tests_required: a finding that does not survive verification is DROPPED and the drop is recorded with a reason
the verifier receives the anchor and the source, never the auditor's prose - a verifier reading the auditor's argument is not independent
both-states control: a genuine defect is CONFIRMED, so the verifier is not dropping everything
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the surface-auditor, which may contest a drop with new evidence but not with repetition
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:UX-7903 emitted only when the finding is CONFIRMED or DROPPED with a reason, never left unadjudicated; otherwise FAILED:UX-7903 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then escalate the finding as CONTESTED rather than letting the verifier decide by fatigue
work_unit.mechanism: per-finding adversarial re-derivation with recorded drops
work_unit.not_a_duplicate_because: the surface audit RAISES findings from a whole surface; this adjudicates ONE finding from its anchor with no access to the raising argument

body.title: An unverified finding may not reach the queue

stages.title: The queue contains only findings that survived verification
S3 - rank the survivors into a fix queue

work_unit.title: Rank surviving findings into an implementable fix queue
work_unit.question_or_target: Order confirmed findings by severity times the number of surfaces they affect, and report the survival rate alongside, so the queue's credibility is visible with it.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: severity times reach is a product judgement, not an arithmetic one

work_unit.evidence_requirement: each queue entry carries its file:line anchors, its severity, its affected-surface count and its verification record
tests_required: the queue reports raw findings, confirmed findings and the survival rate together
UNAUDITED surfaces appear in the report as an explicit coverage gap, not as zero findings
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: one independent adversarial reviewer in a fresh context who samples five queue entries and re-checks their anchors
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:UX-7904 emitted only when the queue is ordered, every entry is anchored, and the survival rate plus the UNAUDITED list are both present; otherwise FAILED:UX-7904 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then emit the unranked confirmed set rather than an invented ordering
work_unit.mechanism: severity-times-reach ranking published together with the verification survival rate

stages.title: The shared completion predicate over the audit

impact.blast_radius: read-only over app source; Edit and every app write path are denied, so a 300-agent sweep cannot modify what it audits

worked_example.scenario: Pre-release sweep of an app with 61 surfaces, 9 of them behind feature flags that no click path reaches.
expected_trace: enumerate-surfaces -> 61 surfaces including all 9 flag-gated ones; 3 marked unanalysable (dynamic component factory)
audit-surfaces -> 58 audited, 3 UNAUDITED with reasons; 214 raw findings; barrier quorum 0.95
verify-findings -> 214 verified individually; 78 CONFIRMED, 136 DROPPED with reasons; survival rate 0.36
verified-gate PASS (0 unverified in queue, drops recorded)
rank-fix-queue -> 78 entries ordered by severity x reach; the report carries 214/78/0.36 and the 3 UNAUDITED surfaces
worked_example.expected_terminal_state: SUCCESS:UX-7904 with 78 of 214 findings surviving and 3 surfaces declared UNAUDITED

bp7.unverified: UNVERIFIED as a reusable app-neutral blueprint - the survival rate is recorded from two executed runs on two apps, and a third would test whether the shape or the app determines it. Settling experiment = run on a third app and compare the verified-finding survival rate against the two recorded runs.

distinct_from.bp-ux-02: that audits the RUNNING app and can measure computed contrast; this audits SOURCE and reaches surfaces the runtime cannot
distinct_from.BP-CNC-04: that gives reviewers a sibling's full text; this gives a verifier only an anchor, deliberately withholding the raising argument
distinct_from.bp-ux-01: no design direction, no revert gate - this produces a queue, not a change

bp7.flagship_rationale: NOT flagship: an end-to-end test needs a real multi-surface app source tree with a router, which this repo does not contain. Its structural properties (a second fan-out over findings, UNAUDITED accounting, verified-only queue) ARE asserted by test_bp7_slice.py.
